title: Vector schema negotiation + hot-swap migration for embedding dim changes
creator: Priya Khatri
description:
Summary:
This ticket scopes and schedules engineering work to support safe, low-latency migrations when an embedding model changes vector dimensionality (e.g., 1024 -> 1536) or when we introduce an alternative schema (dense vs. sparse components). Goals: preserve client compatibility, avoid service disruption for live indexes, provide a transparent negotiation layer so clients and SDKs can adapt without immediate reindex, and provide an automated hot-swap reindex path with observability and rollback controls.

What we're solving:
- Model providers and internal model upgrades will occasionally change output dimension. Current index store expects a fixed dimension which forces full reindex or client-side shims. Full reindex is expensive and often not feasible for large customer datasets.
- Client SDKs may send vectors of an older dimension; run-time rejects are customer-visible errors.
- Reranking endpoints that rely on exact dot-product or cosine behave differently across dims; we must ensure scoring consistency or provide documented equivalences.

High-level approach:
1) Schema negotiation: introduce a lightweight header in embed/rerank API (X-Embed-Dim, X-Embed-Schema) to surface incoming vector metadata. Server accepts multiple dims for a period and routes to compatibility adapters.
2) Compatibility adapters: server-side runtime supports two compatibility modes: projection and proxy-match. Projection uses learned or heuristic projection matrices (fast, approximate). Proxy-match uses hybrid index lookups that translate queries into the target index space via mapping vectors stored in a small transform index.
3) Hot-swap reindex: behind feature flag start a nearline reindex pipeline that re-embeds items in the background using streaming snapshot and per-shard copy-on-write. New index is validated via sampling and A/B reroutes and then atomically switched when validation passes.
4) Client SDKs & docs: SDKs will surface a deprecation warning when server supports different dims and provide a one-line migration snippet.
5) Metrics & safety: design canary metrics (P99 latency, 99th-run rerank divergence, top-1 flip rate) and a backout plan if score regression or latency exceeds thresholds.

Trade-offs considered:
- Projection (fast) vs exact reindex (accurate/costly). We will offer projection as interim with explicit accuracy SLAs and require reindex for long-term parity.
- On-the-fly translation increases CPU and memory during migration windows; mitigated with autoscale and a heuristic to only translate for top-k rerank candidates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Server accepts requests with X-Embed-Dim header for legacy and new dims and routes through adapter without 500-level errors.
- Canary rollout shows <2% top-1 flip rate vs baseline on selected test-set and P95 latency increase <10ms for rerank requests in canary.
- Nearline reindex can rebuild a 100M-item index (10B total embedding bytes) in under 72 hours on a dedicated reindex pool (target benchmark).
- SDKs updated with migration helper and automated deprecation warnings published in release notes.
decision_summary: We will implement a two-stage migration path. Stage 1 = negotiation + server-side projection adapter that gives immediate compatibility and reduces customer error rates. Stage 2 = background hot-swap reindex for final parity. Projection is designated as temporary with monitoring and automated prompts to customers to reindex. Chosen because it minimizes customer downtime while bounding cost and implementation complexity.
rollout_plan: Feature flag off in prod for initial rollout: enable in staging
Deploy negotiation header parsing and acceptance (no-op path) - smoke tests
Enable projection adapter in staging; run synthetic eval suite (embedding similarity, rerank replay)
Canary: 5% traffic to adapter path in us-west, monitor metrics for 48h
If canary OK, increase to 25% for 72h with autoscaling enabled
Enable nearline reindex pipeline for internal test dataset; validate correctness
Perform atomic hot-swap on a small customer sandbox; observe behavioral metrics
Open customer communications and SDK release, announce migration window
Full rollout with scheduled reindex pool; provide backout steps and support runbook
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: Embed-Dim Negotiation - count of mismatched-dim requests, adapter CPU/memory, P95 latency
Quality metrics: top-1 flip rate, nDCG@10 delta, calibration drift per model version
Alerts: top-1 flip rate >3% sustained for 15m; P95 latency regression >20ms for rerank route
Automated revert: if critical alert triggers, route 100% traffic to legacy index and pause reindex
Postmortem checklist: collect sample query IDs, reroot to reindex snapshots, escalate to ML research for projection tuning
test_plan: Unit: negotiation parsing, header validation, adapter fallthrough paths
Integration: end-to-end rerank with legacy vs projected embeddings on replayed traffic
Performance: loadtest 10k QPS with 5% adapter usage, measure tail latencies
Canary validation: compute nDCG@10 and top-1 flip rate against golden dataset
Chaos: simulate partial shard availability during hot-swap and verify backout
comments: 2026-03-10 - Priya Khatri: Created ticket after PM sync with Growth customers who requested model upgrade path.
2026-03-11 - Diego Alvarez: Prototype projection adapter implemented (PR link above). Early local sims show 92% top-1 agreement for 1024->1536 projection using linear PCA-based fit.
2026-03-12 - ML Research (Aisha Morgan): Ran evaluation across 10k queries; noted failure modes on nearest-neighbor boundary cases. Proposed fallback to proxy-match for low-confidence queries.
2026-03-13 - Security (Evan Wu): Confirmed no extra PII handling required; reindex pipeline will run inside dedicated VPC by default.
2026-03-13 - Diego Alvarez: Added canary thresholds and instrumentation. Scheduling reindex infra work with infra team for 2026-03-20.
notes: Follow-on tickets will break out: (a) SDK warning & migration helper, (b) Autoscale/Governor rules for adapter CPU pressure, (c) Customer-facing migration schedule tool in Console. We should also coordinate with Sales for high-volume customers and offer managed reindex bundles.
